# Evidence

Proof-of-work for the end-to-end flow: **a goal -> a genuine LLM-driven
discovery run -> a saved capability artifact -> deterministic replay ->
human escalation and handoff**. Every folder here is a real run against
the live fake app (`src/cua/fake_app/`); nothing is hand-authored.

One scenario per runtime condition the brief names in Section 3.3, plus
"outright app errors" from Section 1, plus the success, identity and
handoff cases. Every scenario ended where it was expected to.

| Scenario | Brief | Expected | Actual | Exit | Folder |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `success_10001` | 3.3 replay + outputs | `success` | success | `0` | [`success_10001/`](success_10001/) |
| `success_10002` | 3.3 replay + outputs | `success` | success | `0` | [`success_10002/`](success_10002/) |
| `not_found` | 3.3 expected business outcome | `business_outcome member_not_found` | business_outcome member_not_found | `2` | [`not_found/`](not_found/) |
| `invalid_input` | 3.3 validation error | `hard_failure input_invalid` | hard_failure input_invalid | `1` | [`invalid_input/`](invalid_input/) |
| `popup_recovered` | 3.3 unexpected dialog | `recovered` | recovered | `0` | [`popup_recovered/`](popup_recovered/) |
| `session_expired_recovered` | 3.3 session timeout | `recovered` | recovered | `0` | [`session_expired_recovered/`](session_expired_recovered/) |
| `slow_load_ok` | 3.3 transient slowness | `success` | success | `0` | [`slow_load_ok/`](slow_load_ok/) |
| `slow_load_timeout` | 3.3 slow/failed load | `hard_failure timeout` | hard_failure timeout | `1` | [`slow_load_timeout/`](slow_load_timeout/) + `failure.png` |
| `permission_denied` | 3.3 permission denial | `business_outcome permission_denied` | business_outcome permission_denied | `2` | [`permission_denied/`](permission_denied/) |
| `app_error` | 3.3 / 1 app error | `hard_failure app_error` | hard_failure app_error | `1` | [`app_error/`](app_error/) + `failure.png` |
| `wrong_member` | 3.3 hard failure (identity) | `hard_failure identity_mismatch` | hard_failure identity_mismatch | `1` | [`wrong_member/`](wrong_member/) + `failure.png` |
| `duplicate_abandon` | 3.6 escalation | `needs_human ambiguous_duplicate` | needs_human ambiguous_duplicate | `3` | [`duplicate_abandon/`](duplicate_abandon/) |
| `duplicate_takeover` | 3.6 take control of the live session | `recovered` | recovered | `0` | [`duplicate_takeover/`](duplicate_takeover/) |
| `risky_step_approved` | 3.6 + 3.4 risky step approved | `recovered` | recovered | `0` | [`risky_step_approved/`](risky_step_approved/) |

**Expected** is what the scenario declares it should do. **Actual** is read
back out of the run's own `result.json` afterwards. They are separate
columns on purpose: a table whose result column is filled in from what the
runner intended cannot disagree with itself, which is the only thing it is
for.

Each folder holds `command.txt` (how to reproduce that exact run),
`result.json` (the `ReplayResult`, masked), `run.log`, and `failure.png`
where the run failed. Per-step screenshots go to the git-ignored
`evidence/runs/` instead -- committing eight images per scenario would be a
hundred PNGs nobody opens, and the one that carries information is the
state a failure ended in.

```
python scripts/run_evidence.py                    # all scenarios
python scripts/run_evidence.py --only app_error   # just one
python scripts/run_evidence.py --list
```

The credential is parameterized in every `command.txt` as
`$env:TELLER_PASSWORD`; its value is in the top-level
[README](../README.md) and appears in no file under `evidence/`.

Most scenarios run the replay CLI as a real subprocess, so the command in
the folder is literally what ran and the exit code is a real process exit
status. `duplicate_abandon`, `duplicate_takeover`, `risky_step_approved` run in-process instead,
because they need a *programmable* operator and the CLI deliberately offers
only human handoff modes (`--handoff terminal|interactive`); their exit
codes come from the same table the CLI uses, and their `command.txt` gives
the interactive equivalent.

## Not produced by that script

| Folder | What it shows |
| --- | --- |
| [`discovery-member-lookup/`](discovery-member-lookup/) | The **required** genuine LLM-driven run: `claude-sonnet-5`, via `browser_toolset_20260801`, really drives the browser through login -> search -> read balance. Full step log plus screenshots. Not a replay scenario, so `run_evidence.py` does not re-run it. |
| [`extra_row/`](extra_row/) | Three replays of the **same page** with one extra row inserted, differing only in the artifact: position-only locators return `success` with a **date in the savings balance**; label-anchored locators return the right figure; a declared `money` type catches the same shifted value as a second layer. Frozen -- the comparison *is* the evidence. |
| [`stability/`](stability/) | 20 replays against injected faults, scored for **wrong answers** (values that aren't the requested member's) and for outcomes that didn't match their fault. Produced by `scripts/run_stability.py`. |

The capability artifacts live in [`/artifacts/`](../artifacts/) -- every
replay above executes one of those exact files.

## What's *not* here: `runs/`

`evidence/runs/` is git-ignored scratch. Every scenario points its
`--evidence-dir` there, so per-step screenshots and intermediate captures
land somewhere that isn't committed.
